Agricultural products trade

Malawi-grown agricultural products for buyers worldwide

Sycamore Agritech Limited is based in Lilongwe, Malawi. Drawing on our own farms and a network of local growers, we source and supply Malawi-grown agricultural products to customers at home and abroad: pulses, oilseeds, nuts, grains, spices and specialty products. From sourcing, grading and packing to export documents and transport, we take care of the Malawi end.

Why buy from us

A reliable partner on the ground in Malawi

Buying farm produce from thousands of kilometres away, the worries are the same everywhere: goods that do not match the sample, missing paperwork and late shipments. We are at the origin, and we solve those problems for you.

Grown in Malawi, supplied at origin

Our supply comes from our own farms and from Malawian growers we work with season after season; every lot is recorded with its origin, batch and supplier.

Every lot checked before it ships

Lots are sampled and checked against the contract: moisture, foreign matter and grading. For groundnuts and similar products we provide aflatoxin test reports from an accredited laboratory, and third-party pre-shipment inspection (for example SGS) can be arranged on request.

Export paperwork done by us

Export licence, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, customs declaration and the Reserve Bank export declaration are all completed on the Malawi side, so you receive one complete set of documents.

Preferential market access

As goods of Malawian origin from a least-developed country, our products enter China tariff-free and the European Union and United Kingdom duty-free and quota-free, with SADC, COMESA and AfCFTA preferences within Africa.

Availability

When each product is available

Rain-fed crops in Malawi are mostly harvested from April to June, so new-crop supply is at its best from June to September; tree crops follow their own cycles. The chart shows the harvest and new-crop supply periods of our main products.

How we work

From enquiry to delivery in six steps

We follow the usual practice of international commodity trade, and keep every step clear.

  1. Enquiry

    Tell us the product, specification, quantity, destination port and preferred Incoterm.

  2. Offer & samples

    We send an offer and a representative sample for your evaluation.

  3. Contract & payment

    We agree specification, packing, delivery time and payment terms, and sign the sales contract.

  4. Sourcing, grading & packing

    We source, clean, grade and pack the goods in Malawi to the contract.

  5. Inspection & documents

    Pre-shipment inspection, then export licence, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin and customs clearance.

  6. Shipment & tracking

    Goods travel overland to the port and are shipped; we track the consignment and send you the full document set.

Trade terms

We quote EXW Lilongwe, FCA/FOB Beira or Nacala, or CFR/CIF your destination port (Incoterms® 2020).

Payment

For new customers, usually an irrevocable letter of credit at sight; for repeat business, a telegraphic-transfer deposit with the balance against shipping documents. Terms are set in each contract.

Packing

25 kg or 50 kg woven PP bags or 1-tonne big bags; vacuum packing for kernels on request; shipped as full 20-foot container loads.

Minimum order

Usually one 20-foot container; smaller trial lots are possible for some products.

Samples

Representative samples can be couriered before you commit to a contract.

Inspection

Third-party pre-shipment inspection (for example SGS) can be arranged on request; moisture, foreign matter and aflatoxin results are reported by an accredited laboratory.

Logistics

From landlocked Malawi to ports worldwide

Malawi is landlocked: goods travel by road or rail to ports in Mozambique, Tanzania or South Africa. We choose the corridor that suits your destination, the season and the volume.

Nacala, Mozambique

Nacala corridor

Rail from the Kanengo railhead in Lilongwe straight to the deep-water port of Nacala, about 1,000 km, with a road alternative. Well suited to full-container bulk cargo.

Beira, Mozambique

Beira corridor

About 950 km by road via Dedza and Tete to the port of Beira, one of Malawi's main gateways, with regular sailings to Asia, the Middle East and Europe.

Dar es Salaam, Tanzania

Dar es Salaam corridor

North through the Songwe border crossing, about 1,700 km, an alternative route for East Asia and the Gulf.

Lilongwe airport (LLW)

Air freight

Samples and small lots of perishable produce fly from Kamuzu International Airport, Lilongwe, with connections via Addis Ababa or Nairobi.

Transit times depend on the corridor, the season and sailing schedules; Durban is a further option. Every offer states the proposed route and the expected delivery time.

Export documents

Complete paperwork for smooth clearance

Every consignment ships with the documents below, prepared to the requirements of the destination country and the letter of credit.

  • Phytosanitary certificateIssued after inspection by Malawi's plant protection authority, the Department of Agricultural Research Services (DARS).
  • Certificate of originIssued by the Malawi Confederation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MCCCI); SADC and COMESA preferential certificates by the Malawi Revenue Authority.
  • Quality and test reportsGrade, moisture, foreign-matter and aflatoxin reports from an accredited laboratory or a third-party inspection company.
  • Fumigation certificateContainer or stack fumigation with a certificate, where the destination country requires it.
  • Commercial invoice and packing listMatching the contract, with HS codes, net and gross weights, bag counts and lot numbers.
  • Transport documentsOcean bill of lading or road consignment note; the export licence and customs declaration are handled by us in Malawi.

FAQ

Importing from Malawi: common questions

What is the minimum order quantity (MOQ)?

Usually one 20-foot container. For some products we accept smaller trial lots; just ask.

Can you send samples first?

Yes. Before any contract we can courier a representative sample, and the shipment is supplied to the agreed specification.

Which payment terms do you accept?

New customers usually pay by irrevocable letter of credit at sight; established customers by telegraphic-transfer deposit with the balance against shipping documents.

What is the lead time from order to shipment?

It depends on the product, the season and the corridor. Once the deposit or letter of credit is in place we confirm a schedule for sourcing, inspection, documents and inland transport, and every offer states the expected delivery time.

Can you arrange third-party inspection?

Yes. On request we arrange pre-shipment inspection and loading supervision by SGS or a similar company, with the cost shown in the offer.

Are there export restrictions on agricultural products in Malawi?

Yes. Some products, such as maize, soybeans and sugar, need a government export licence and may face seasonal restrictions. We confirm the current rules before signing and only commit to goods that can legally be exported.
